review.overview: PR #403 (head 143990e) stages a shared Railway Redis queue and moves scraper queue code behind a new `@package/queue` package. The diagram shows only edges that exist in the relationship catalog. In `.railway/railway.ts`, the legacy `scraper-queue` Redis and the new `pocket-trash-queue` Redis are both declared. `redis-volume` is declared as a separate resource. The scraper service declares `REDIS_URL: preserve()`. In scraper code, `createScraperQueues` calls `createBullMqQueueAdapter`, and the adapter builds an ioredis `Redis` connection from `redisUrl`. The sources do not show that `REDIS_URL` resolves to the new queue. Docs and the preview deploy workflow disagree about the current target, and the catalog has no edge for either. Those links are therefore left out of the diagram.

changedAreas.summary: Declares `legacyScraperQueue` as redis("scraper-queue") (lines 26-28, comment: retained until a separately approved cleanup). Declares `sharedQueue` as redis("pocket-trash-queue") (lines 39-41, comment: provisioned additively). The shared queue's start command adds `--appendonly yes --appendfsync everysec` (line 44). `redisVolume` is declared as volume("redis-volume") (lines 51-56). The scraper service declares `REDIS_URL: preserve()` (line 103). The `project(...)` resources list at line 117 holds all four resources. The file contains no binding between the volume and either Redis resource, and none between `REDIS_URL` and a specific Redis. Resource-list membership and names do not establish either.

`createScraperQueues(redisUrl, adapter = createBullMqQueueAdapter({ redisUrl }))` at queues.ts:297-300 calls `adapter.define` for the items queue (lines 301-306) and the images queue (lines 307-312). It closes through `adapter.close()` (line 320). `createScraperJobContext` in jobs.ts passes `env.REDIS_URL` to `createRedisConnection` (line 118) and to `createScraperQueues` (line 129). The catalog does not link the queues.ts:299 call expression to the adapter definition in bullmq.ts, so that edge is not drawn.

bullmq.ts:23-82 defines `createBullMqQueueAdapter`. It creates `new Redis(options.redisUrl, ...)` (lines 33-46) and wraps each definition in a `BullMqDefinedQueue` (lines 73-78). The adapter's `define` registers it with `queues.add` (line 78). The ADR (decisions/architecture/eng-497-shared-queue-boundary.md:12-25) says the package owns BullMQ and ioredis in production, with a deterministic in-memory adapter for tests, and that physical scraper queue names stay compatible during migration. packages/queue/src/index.ts (the contract), test-contract.ts and the tests were not rendered as edges.

docs/railway.md:104-134 says the checked-in stage retains both Redis resources and authorizes no provisioning or switching. docs/railway.md:274-276 says the preview workflow keeps using `scraper-queue` until an approved cutover. docs/railway.md:206-209 and docs/environment-variables.md:46 say `REDIS_URL` should reference `${{pocket-trash-queue.REDIS_URL}}`. .github/workflows/deploy.yml:30 sets `RAILWAY_SCRAPER_QUEUE_PREVIEW_SERVICE_NAME: "scraper-queue"`, and lines 664 and 720 build the preview `REDIS_URL` reference from it using `REDIS_PUBLIC_URL`. Test fixtures (env.test.ts:177-189, cli.test.ts:64) use the `pocket-trash-queue` reference string. This is documented intent and fixtures, not a verified runtime connection.

docs/infrastructure-diagram.yaml and docs/infrastructure-diagram.eraser add `prod_queue`, `preview_queue` and `dev_queue` nodes. They add scraper-to-queue edges labeled `scraper-images / scraper-items` in production and `scraper queues` in preview and dev. They also add an `@package/queue` workspace dependency from the scraper. These edges are documentation only. They are not in the relationship catalog and are not drawn.

Adds railpack.json, `.railwayignore` entries, a `RAILPACK_INSTALL_CMD` variable set in deploy.yml (patch lines 5-10 and 19-24), and an `RAILPACK_INSTALL_CMD` entry in the scraper env. Also updates scripts/check-railway-context.mjs, scripts/classify-changes.mjs and their tests, and adds two changesets. These are described but not drawn, because the catalog has no call edges for them.

review.overview: PR #354 (head 0c3e8fe) adds a Pens catalog schema to the database package. It covers Pen products, Pen-part subtypes, refill products, configuration slots and choices, collection-item detail tables, refill offerings, compatibility assertions, and market and source-evidence tables. The PR also changes catalog alias scoping. The new Drizzle tables are in packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts. They hang off product and collection_item in schema/collection.ts. A migration, relation wiring, schema exports, docs, integration tests and the catalog service are updated alongside. Three diagrams follow. One schema-domain flowchart maps the product, collection and refill links. One ER slice covers Pen product subtypes and the configuration choice graph. A second ER slice covers refill compatibility with market and source evidence, because it is a separate domain with its own evidence and market links. All relationships come from FK declarations in review-relationships.json. The host derives PK/FK markers and cardinalities from nullability and unique/PK flags. The catalogue omitted 652 nodes and 373 relationships, so every diagram is a slice.

ER slice: refill compatibility, market containment and source evidence

changedAreas.summary: New file of about 1,400 lines. Product-owned shared-PK detail tables (product_detail_pen, _pen_part, _refill) have id referencing product.id (pens.ts:52-55, 68-77, 129-148). The clip, tip, top-cap, mechanism and actuator tables also reference product_detail_pen_part.id from the same id column (pens.ts:80-126). product_detail_refill adds a composite FK (id, maker_id) to product (id, maker_id) at pens.ts:139-143. Collection-side shared-PK tables use collectionDetailId, referencing collection_item.id (pens.ts:62-65).

product_configuration_slot references product and configuration_slot_kind (pens.ts:346-351). product_configuration_choice has three nullable carriers: part_product_id (pens.ts:387-390), product_material_id (402-406) and finish_option_id (407-411). A CHECK uses num_nonnulls(...) = 1 over the three (pens.ts:434-437). The choice also has a composite FK to its slot (pens.ts:394-401). Rule and requirement tables chain from the choice through composite (id, product_id) FKs (pens.ts:460-467, 500-515).

changedAreas.area: Refill offerings, collection detail and selections (pens.ts:557-741)
changedAreas.summary: refill_offering references product_detail_refill (pens.ts:557-559). collection_detail_pen references collection_item, product_detail_pen, an optional installed refill product and an optional refill offering via composite FK (pens.ts:601-620). Clip, tip, top-cap, mechanism and actuator collection-detail tables share the collection_item id and reference their product-side part table (pens.ts:640-708). collection_item_configuration_selection references collection_item, an optional installed part collection item and the chosen product_configuration_choice (pens.ts:722-741).

catalog_market_containment has parent and child FKs to catalog_market (pens.ts:779-784). catalog_source_evidence has optional listing_id (pens.ts:831-834) and optional market_id (844-847). product_source_listing uses listing_id as its PK, so each listing links to one product (pens.ts:870-875). catalog_source_listing_choice is a composite-PK junction between listing and choice (pens.ts:884-891). catalog_source_image links a listing to product_image (pens.ts:904-909). refill_offering_evidence links an offering to evidence (pens.ts:936-941).

refill_compatibility_group_membership is the junction between refill_compatibility_group and product_detail_refill (pens.ts:1121-1126). refill_compatibility_assertion references a Pen and has optional required-tip, target-group and target-refill FKs (pens.ts:1146-1158). A CHECK requires exactly one of target group or target refill (pens.ts:1196-1199). refill_compatibility_evidence has optional pen, tip and refill FKs (pens.ts:1241-1251). Assertion-evidence and membership-evidence junctions point to assertions or memberships and to evidence (pens.ts:1298-1335).

collection_item gains serial_number. product gains product_id_maker_unique (id, maker_id) and a maker index. product_material and finish_option gain (id, product_id) unique keys, which the new composite FKs reference. catalog_terminology_alias now has a nullable maker_id, a concept_id plus canonical_namespace composite FK to catalog_terminology_concept (id, namespace), and scope/preferred constraints (collection.ts patch lines 29-109). That alias-to-concept FK is not in the relationship catalogue.

The new migration (migration.sql, 1,145 lines) defines constraint triggers (e.g. validate_pens_product_detail at lines 715-772, evidence-support triggers at 1049-1058, market conflict triggers at 1131-1133). schema/relations.ts adds about 587 lines of relation wiring. schema/index.ts and src/index.ts export the new schema and the PensSchemaRows and NewPensSchemaRows types. docs/database-schema-diagram.html is updated. snapshot.json was omitted from the frozen evidence as a generated file.

packages/services/src/db/catalog/index.ts renames the alias unique-constraint message key to catalog_terminology_alias_scope_value_unique. Alias create looks up catalogTerminologyConcept by namespace and key and writes conceptId. Alias list joins catalogTerminologyConcept. Tests changed: pens-catalog.integration.test.ts (new), fresh-baseline.integration.test.ts, material-specifics.integration.test.ts, and the services catalog integration test.

review.overview: PR #354 (feat(database): add Pens catalog schema) introduces packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts as a new Pens catalog schema domain atop the existing collection schema. The head SHA evidence (0c3e8fe0d5cd58f2841f479cdeffd901b416f4fb) shows pens.ts declaring shared-primary-key product detail subtypes (product_detail_pen pens.ts:68, product_detail_pen_part pens.ts:74, pen_clip pens.ts:80, pen_tip pens.ts:88, pen_top_cap pens.ts:96, pen_mechanism pens.ts:104, pen_actuator pens.ts:121, product_detail_refill pens.ts:129), a terminology concept layer (catalog_terminology_concept pens.ts:161, product_alias pens.ts:209, pen_part_role_assignment pens.ts:240, pen_nose_profile_assignment pens.ts:268), a product configuration slot/choice/rule system (pens.ts:323-520), refill offerings and evidence (pens.ts:523-1114), catalog market containment (pens.ts:752-794), catalog source listings and evidence (pens.ts:797-930), and refill compatibility groups, assertions and evidence (pens.ts:1117-1348). Collection-side changes in packages/database/src/schema/collection.ts add shared-PK slider and spinner subtype tables (collection.ts:1022-1166) and a finish_option family (collection.ts:691-782). The visual catalog below maps the new pens domain and two focused entity-relationship slices; the host derives PK/FK markers and cardinalities from the frozen relationship catalog (review-relationships.json, visual-relationships-v1).

review.overview: PR #376 adds material Trends drill-downs. Its database layer adds one table, public_collection_item_material_trend, and one column, public_trends_generation.has_suppressed_material_values. The services layer gets two readers: exact catalog-product material counts from live tables, and rounded, privacy-suppressed counts from the active generation. Two server functions in catalog-api.ts expose these. The /trends route loader fetches both datasets next to the existing ones and passes them to TrendsPage. The relationship catalogue contains no entity-to-entity foreign-key edges for the four Trends tables, so the ER diagram shows the four changed entities without relationship lines. The FKs are described in changedAreas instead, with line anchors.

diagrams.title: Changed Trends entities (no catalogued FK edges)

changedAreas.summary: New table public_collection_item_material_trend (lines 52-104) has a single-column PK id. Its columns include generation_id (NOT NULL) and nullable product_type_id, material_id and material_specific_id. Lines 61, 66 and 71 document the null cases: headline aggregate, Unspecified bucket, and general-material or Unspecified buckets. public_trends_generation (lines 16-49) gains has_suppressed_material_values (lines 39-42). The existing public_part_accessory_product_type_trend (lines 107-126) and public_collection_item_product_type_trend (lines 129-150) each use a composite PK of (generation_id, product_type_id) at lines 120 and 144.

changedAreas.area: Declared foreign keys (not drawn in the diagram)
changedAreas.summary: Source declares these FKs. generation_id references public_trends_generation.id with ON DELETE CASCADE in all three child tables (trends.ts:58-60, 110-112, 132-134). product_type_id references productType.id with ON DELETE RESTRICT (trends.ts:62-65, 113-115, 135-137). On the material table, product_type_id and material_id are nullable FKs (trends.ts:62-70). material_id references material.id with RESTRICT (trends.ts:67-70). A composite FK (material_id, material_specific_id) references materialSpecific(material_id, id) with RESTRICT (trends.ts:98-102). The referenced tables come from ./scraper.js (trends.ts:13), which is not in the supplied evidence.

changedAreas.area: Constraints on the new material table
changedAreas.summary: A unique index (trends.ts:83-89) covers generation_id, coalesce(product_type_id,0), coalesce(material_id,0), coalesce(material_specific_id,0) and is_specific_breakdown. Two CHECK constraints sit at trends.ts:90-97. One requires counts to be positive multiples of 5. The other requires material_id to be non-null whenever material_specific_id is non-null. public_trends_generation also has a partial unique index on active where active is true (trends.ts:45-47).

Creates the material trend table (lines 1-12), adds the has_suppressed_material_values column (line 14), creates the scope unique index (line 15), and adds four FK constraints (lines 16-19). The SQL names the targets as public_trends_generation, product_types, materials and material_specific. snapshot.json was omitted from the evidence as a generated file.

Adds PublicMaterialTrend and PublicCollectionMaterialTrends types (patch lines 5-39). getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends (patch lines 57-136) runs a raw SQL grouping-sets query over product, product_types and product_material. getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends (patch lines 145-221) reads the active public_trends_generation row, then joins public_collection_item_material_trend to material and materialSpecific. The refresh transaction (patch lines 230-344) computes material counts across the collection_detail_* tables and filters them by the contributor threshold. It sets hasSuppressedMaterialValues, rounds counts, and inserts rows into the material trend table.

catalog-api.ts adds createServerFn wrappers getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends and getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends (1-patch lines 5-19). Each calls s.db.trends.* through a dynamic import of @/lib/services. routes/trends.tsx extends the loader's Promise.all to five calls (8-patch lines 22-34). It passes catalogMaterialTrends, collectionMaterialTrends and a search object to TrendsPage, replacing onProductTypeChange and selectedProductTypeId with onSearchChange and search (8-patch lines 60-77).

The changeset .changeset/warm-materials-trend.md marks minor bumps for @app/web, @package/database and @package/services. review.overview: PR #376 adds material Trends drill-downs to the Pocket-Trash application. The change introduces a new database table public_collection_item_material_trend for storing privacy-transformed material counts, adds a has_suppressed_material_values flag to the trends generation table, and implements corresponding UI components, API routes, and service methods. The schema supports nullable foreign keys to product types, materials, and material specifics, enabling aggregate headline rows and unspecified material buckets.

diagrams.title: Trends Schema Entity Relationships

changedAreas.summary: New table public_collection_item_material_trend created with PK id bigint, FK generation_id bigint NOT NULL referencing public_trends_generation.id with CASCADE delete, nullable FKs to product_types, materials, and composite FK to material_specific. Added has_suppressed_material_values column to public_trends_generation. Unique index on generation scope with coalesced nullable keys. Check constraints validate rounded counts are multiples of 5 and material_specific_id requires material_id.

Added getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends for exact catalog counts and getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends for privacy-safe aggregated data. Service reads from publicTrendsGeneration joined with publicCollectionItemMaterialTrend, left joined to material and materialSpecific tables for name resolution. Stale detection based on 36-hour threshold.

Trends page expanded with material drill-down UI components, route handlers updated with new data loaders, API client methods added for material trend queries. Filter components support material and specific material selection.

TypeScript schema definitions updated in packages/database/src/schema/trends.ts defining publicCollectionItemMaterialTrend table with identity PK starting at 1000, notNull generationId with cascade references, nullable productTypeId, nullable materialId, nullable materialSpecificId with composite foreign key constraint to materialSpecific table via foreignKey helper.

review.overview: PR #354 (head 0c3e8fe) adds a Pens catalog schema to `@package/database`. The new `packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts` defines about 40 tables. They fall into five groups: product subtypes for pens, pen parts and refills; terminology and configuration slots, choices, rules and requirements; refill offerings with market, source and evidence tables; refill compatibility groups, assertions and evidence; and collection-side pen detail and configuration-selection tables. `collection.ts` gains a `serial_number` column and a reshaped `catalog_terminology_alias`. The change also adds migration `20261010021729_pens_catalog_schema`, relation exports, a regenerated schema diagram HTML, database and service integration tests, and a small update to `packages/services/src/db/catalog/index.ts`. The diagrams below cover only entities and foreign keys listed in `review-relationships.json`. The schema-domain flowchart is the wide map. The first ER slice covers the shared-PK product and collection-item subtype structure. The second ER slice covers the configuration slot, choice, rule and selection structure, which uses nullable exclusive carriers.

diagrams.title: Shared-PK Pens subtypes on product and collection_item
Product configuration slots, choices, rules and collection selections

changedAreas.summary: `product_detail_pen`, `product_detail_pen_part`, the five concrete part tables (clip, tip, top cap, mechanism, actuator) and `product_detail_refill` use their `id` as a primary key that is also a foreign key to `product.id` (pens.ts:53-55, 68-143; r16-r29). Each part table also has an `id` foreign key to `product_detail_pen_part` (pens.ts:81, 89, 97, 107, 122). `product_detail_refill` has a second composite foreign key on (id, maker_id) to `product` (pens.ts:139-143, r29). The migration adds deferred constraint triggers named `product_*_consistent`. These check the subtype row against the product type slug, for example a 'pen' product requires a `product_detail_pen` row (migration.sql:715-772).

`collection_detail_pen` and the five concrete part detail tables share the primary key of `collection_item` through an `id` foreign key (pens.ts:63-65, 597-710; r46, r50, r52, r54, r56, r58). Each also holds a foreign key to its catalog counterpart: `product_detail_pen`, `_clip`, `_tip`, `_top_cap`, `_mechanism` or `_actuator` (r47, r51, r53, r55, r57, r59). `collection_detail_pen` has an optional installed refill foreign key and an optional composite (offering, refill product) foreign key (pens.ts:604-620, r48-r49). Constraint triggers `collection_detail_*_consistent` require exactly one Pens detail row per `collection_item` that has one (migration.sql:774-798).

`catalog_terminology_concept` has a referenced unique key on (id, namespace) (pens.ts:173). `product_alias` links to `product` (pens.ts:213-215, r30). `pen_part_role_assignment` and `pen_nose_profile_assignment` use composite (concept_id, namespace) foreign keys to the concept table (pens.ts:251-258, 278-285; r32, r34). `refill_compatibility_group` has a unique foreign key to the concept table (pens.ts:306-314, r35). In collection.ts, `catalog_terminology_alias` now has a nullable `maker_id` and a `concept_id` composite foreign key to `catalog_terminology_concept` (collection.ts:577-632, 4-patch.txt:46-102). Its canonical-key reference to `product_types.slug` is removed in the same patch. A nose-profile carrier trigger limits `pen_nose_profile_assignment` to products of type 'pen' or 'pen-tip' (migration.sql:800-812).

changedAreas.area: Configuration slots, choices, rules and collection selections
changedAreas.summary: `product_configuration_slot` references `product` and `configuration_slot_kind` (pens.ts:346-351, r36-r37). `product_configuration_choice` has nullable foreign keys to `product_detail_pen_part`, `product_material` and `finish_option`. The latter two are composite (id, product_id) keys. A check requires exactly one of the three carrier columns to be non-null (pens.ts:387-411, 434-437; r38, r40, r41). Rules and requirements chain through composite (id, product_id) keys (pens.ts:460-515, r42-r44). `collection_item_configuration_selection` has a primary key on (collection_item_id, slot_id). It references `collection_item` twice, once required and once optional, and references the choice on (choice_id, slot_id) (pens.ts:722-741, 733; r60-r62). Deferred triggers validate product configuration and collection selections (migration.sql:844-966). Supporting unique constraints on `product_material` and `finish_option` are added in collection.ts (4-patch.txt:38-43, 105-109).

`catalog_market_containment` has a composite primary key (parent_market_id, child_market_id) and two foreign keys to `catalog_market` (pens.ts:776-790, r63-r64). `catalog_source_evidence` has optional foreign keys to `catalog_source_listing` and `catalog_market` (pens.ts:831-847, r65-r66). `product_source_listing` references `product` and has a unique foreign key to the listing (pens.ts:870-875, r67-r68). `catalog_source_listing_choice` and `catalog_source_image` link listings to choices and product images (pens.ts:884-909, r69-r72). Refill offering, market-status and identifier tables carry versioned lifecycle and successor data, and evidence link tables use composite primary keys (pens.ts:933-1114). A trigger makes `catalog_source_evidence` append-only (migration.sql:1060-1064), and conflict and support triggers cover refill status, identifiers and market containment (migration.sql:991-1133).

`refill_compatibility_group_membership` references the group and `product_detail_refill` (pens.ts:1121-1126, r77-r78). `refill_compatibility_assertion` references `product_detail_pen` and has optional references to `product_detail_pen_tip`, a group and a refill product (pens.ts:1146-1158, r79-r82). `refill_compatibility_evidence` has optional references to a pen, a tip and a refill (pens.ts:1241-1251, r83-r85). The assertion and membership evidence junctions connect the assertion or membership to the evidence row (pens.ts:1298-1335, r86-r89).

review.overview: PR #354 (feat(database): add Pens catalog schema) introduces the pens catalog in packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts (1407 added lines), a Drizzle migration (packages/database/drizzle/20261010021729_pens_catalog_schema/migration.sql, 1145 lines), relation wiring in packages/database/src/schema/relations.ts, and updates to collection.ts schema, exports, tests, and docs. All relationships below are declared foreign keys anchored in review-relationships.json at head sha 0c3e8fe; cardinalities derive from the cataloged FK nullability and unique constraints (e.g. inverseUnique shared-PK subtypes at pens.ts:53-55, optional carriers at pens.ts:1241-1258).

diagrams.title: Pen part detail ER slice: product_detail_pen and product_detail_pen_part shared-PK subtypes with product_detail_pen_clip, _tip, _top_cap, _mechanism, _actuator carrying product_detail_pen_part keys, plus role and nose-profile assignments referencing catalog_terminology_concept (pens.ts:53-55, 81-99, 243-258, 306-313)

Refill compatibility and source-evidence ER slice (separate high-risk domain): refill_offering to product_detail_refill, catalog_market containment via catalog_market_containment, source listings and evidence to catalog_source_evidence, and compatibility assertions, memberships and their evidence (pens.ts:557-559, 779-784, 831-1335)

changedAreas.summary: New pens catalog schema. product_detail_pen through product_detail_pen_actuator (pens.ts:68-118) and product_detail_refill (pens.ts:139-143) are shared-PK subtypes of product via id references (r16-r29, pens.ts:53-55). pen_part_role_assignment (pens.ts:243-258) links product_detail_pen_part to catalog_terminology_concept via composite concept_id+namespace (r31, r32). product_configuration_slot/choice/rule/requirement (pens.ts:346-515) form a junction-mediated chain: choices reference slots (r39), product_material (r40, optional), and finish_option (r41, optional) through composite keys; rules and requirements reference choices (r42-r44). refill_offering references product_detail_refill (r45, pens.ts:557-559).

collection_detail_pen and its clip/tip/top_cap/mechanism/actuator subtypes share the collection_item primary key (r46, r50, r52, r54, r56, r58) and carry nullable installed-component carriers: collection_detail_pen installs a product_detail_pen (r47), optionally a product_detail_refill (r48) and optionally a refill_offering via composite installed_refill_offering_id+installed_refill_product_id (r49, pens.ts:613-620). collection_item_configuration_selection (pens.ts:722-741) references collection_item twice (r60 required, r61 optional installed part) and product_configuration_choice via composite choice_id+slot_id (r62).

changedAreas.area: packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts compatibility and source evidence cluster (pens.ts:779-1335)
changedAreas.summary: catalog_market_containment junction links parent and child catalog_market rows (r63, r64, pens.ts:779-784); no direct parent-child FK exists on catalog_market itself. catalog_source_evidence optionally references catalog_source_listing and catalog_market (r65, r66). product_source_listing references product and is one-per-listing (r67, r68). catalog_source_listing_choice links listings to configuration choices (r69, r70); catalog_source_image links listings to product_image (r71, r72). refill compatibility evidence flows through refill_offering_evidence (r73, r74), market-status and identifier evidence (r75, r76), and the assertion/membership graph (r77-r89) where refill_compatibility_assertion carries optional tip, group and refill targets (r80-r82, pens.ts:1241-1258).

collection.ts adds finish_option and product-anchored slider detail tables (collection.ts:691-759 finish_option with optional product and per-item unique collection_item carriers r4, r5; finish_option_finish/finish_option_color junction-style PK pairs r7, r8) and slider/spinner detail subtypes (collection.ts:1022-1166, r9-r15). relations.ts adds 587 lines of relation wiring; packages/database/src/index.ts and schema/index.ts export the new pens tables; migration.sql (1145 lines) materializes the DDL including composite FKs and unique keys observed above.

packages/database/test/pens-catalog.integration.test.ts (added, 371 lines), fresh-baseline and material-specifics test updates, packages/services/src/db/catalog/index.ts (+36) and its integration test exercise the new schema; docs/database-schema-diagram.html regenerates the visual catalog (docs are descriptive only, not evidence).

review.overview: PR #376 adds material Trends drill-downs. The database change adds one new table, `public_collection_item_material_trend`, and one new column on `public_trends_generation`. The services layer adds two methods: exact catalog material counts and privacy-safe collection material counts. `catalog-api.ts` exposes both as server functions. The `/trends` route loads them next to the existing trend queries and passes them to `TrendsPage`. Only the four trend tables are in the ER diagram. The relationship catalogue holds no foreign-key relationships for them, so the diagram shows entities and columns without edges.

diagrams.title: Trends schema entities changed in PR 376 (entities only, no catalogued foreign-key edges)

changedAreas.summary: New table `public_collection_item_material_trend` (trends.ts:52-104; migration.sql:1-12). Its primary key is the single column `id`. The columns `product_type_id`, `material_id` and `material_specific_id` are nullable. Trends.ts:61, :66 and :71 describe the nulls as the all-product-types aggregate, the Unspecified bucket, and the general-material or Unspecified bucket. Constraints: a unique index over generation_id, coalesce(product_type_id,0), coalesce(material_id,0), coalesce(material_specific_id,0) and is_specific_breakdown (trends.ts:83-89); a count check requiring rounded counts to be positive multiples of 5 (trends.ts:90-93); and a scope check that `material_specific_id` is null or `material_id` is not null (trends.ts:94-97). `public_trends_generation` gains the non-null column `has_suppressed_material_values` (trends.ts:39-42; migration.sql:14). The same file defines a partial unique index on `active` where `active` is true (trends.ts:45-47). Source declares foreign keys from the new table to the generation table (trends.ts:58-60, cascade delete), `product_type` (trends.ts:62-65, restrict), `material` (trends.ts:67-70, restrict), and a composite key (material_id, material_specific_id) to `material_specific` (material_id, id) (trends.ts:98-102, restrict). The migration declares the same four keys at migration.sql:16-19. The columns are nullable and non-unique, so those would be optional parents with many children. The catalogue omitted these edges, so they are not drawn.

changedAreas.area: Existing trend tables in the same schema file
changedAreas.summary: `public_part_accessory_product_type_trend` (trends.ts:107-126) and `public_collection_item_product_type_trend` (trends.ts:129-150) each have a composite primary key of (generation_id, product_type_id), declared at trends.ts:120 and :144. Each declares non-null foreign keys to the generation table (cascade) and to `product_type` (restrict) at trends.ts:110-115 and :132-137. Both tables appear in the diagram as entities. Their foreign-key edges are not drawn for the same reason.

Adds the exported types `PublicMaterialTrend` and `PublicCollectionMaterialTrends` (13-patch lines 5-39). Adds `getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends`, a raw SQL query that counts approved, non-private products by material and product type (13-patch lines 48-120). It reads `product`, `product_types`, `product_material`, `materials` and `material_specific`, using grouping sets for the general-material and specific-material breakdowns. The collection-side method `getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends` and the refresh logic that writes the new table are in the remaining 227 patch lines of this file, which I did not read. Small export edits in db/index.ts and src/index.ts, and the integration test, were also not read.

changedAreas.area: Web API and route: catalog-api.ts, routes/trends.tsx
changedAreas.summary: `catalog-api.ts` adds server functions `getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends` and `getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends` (1-patch lines 5-19). Both call `s.db.trends.*` through a dynamic import of `@/lib/services`. The `/trends` loader adds both calls to its `Promise.all` (8-patch lines 22-41). `TrendsRoute` passes `catalogMaterialTrends`, `collectionMaterialTrends` and a full `search` object to `TrendsPage`. It replaces the earlier `onProductTypeChange` and `selectedProductTypeId` props with `onSearchChange` and `search` (8-patch lines 60-78).

New `sharedQueue` (`redis("pocket-trash-queue")`, lines 38-49) adds `--appendonly yes --appendfsync everysec` to its start command (line 44) and has a private endpoint `pocket-trash-queue` (line 47). `redisVolume` is declared at lines 50-56. The scraper service at lines 57-114 lists `REDIS_URL: preserve()` at line 103. All four resources are in the `resources` array at line 117. Resource-list membership is a declaration, not an attachment.

Added `packages/queue` (package.json, tsconfig, src/index.ts, src/bullmq.ts, contract tests). `createBullMqQueueAdapter` (packages/queue/src/bullmq.ts:23-82) creates one ioredis `Redis` connection from `options.redisUrl` (line 33). It defines BullMQ queues on that connection (lines 70-80) and closes the queues and disconnects in `close()` (lines 59-63). src/index.ts adds an in-memory adapter, and the contract tests run it alongside the BullMQ adapter. decisions/architecture/eng-497-shared-queue-boundary.md:12-25 documents the transport-independent boundary.

`createScraperQueues(redisUrl, adapter = createBullMqQueueAdapter({ redisUrl }))` (queues.ts:297-324) defines the `items` and `images` queues through `adapter.define` (lines 301-312). It closes through `adapter.close()` (line 320). `createScraperJobContext` (jobs.ts:101-147) calls `createRedisConnection(env.REDIS_URL)` and `redis.ping()` (lines 118-121). It then calls `createScraperQueues(env.REDIS_URL)` (line 129) and closes the queues in `close()` (line 138). The Autmog and Grimsmo producers call `enqueueScraperJobs` (autmog/producer.ts:104; grimsmo/producer.ts:189). queue/processor.ts shrinks by 117 additions and 439 deletions.

review.overview: PR #403 stages a shared Railway queue by introducing a transport-independent queue abstraction at packages/queue. The change provisions a new shared Redis resource (pocket-trash-queue) alongside the retained legacy queue (scraper-queue) in Railway infrastructure. The new package exports createBullMqQueueAdapter for production (wrapping BullMQ/ioredis) and createInMemoryQueueAdapter for tests. Scraper apps migrate from direct BullMQ usage to the adapter pattern via createScraperQueues, which defines typed item and image queues with Zod-validated payloads. Source bindings anchor all connections: railway.ts lines 26-49 declare the Redis resources, packages/queue/src/bullmq.ts lines 23-82 implement the production adapter, and apps/scraper/src/queue/queues.ts lines 297-324 bind scraper definitions to the adapter.

changedAreas.summary: Declares two Redis resources: legacyScraperQueue (retained for migration compatibility) and sharedQueue (new pocket-trash-queue). Configures sharedQueue with appendonly persistence. Declares redisVolume attachment retained without resize. Service configuration preserved with REDIS_URL environment variable.

changedAreas.area: Queue Package Core (packages/queue/src/index.ts lines 276-496, bullmq.ts lines 23-82)
changedAreas.summary: Exports createInMemoryQueueAdapter for deterministic tests and createBullMqQueueAdapter for production. Defines QueueAdapter interface with define() and close() operations. Implements payload validation, retry scheduling, job retention pruning, and continuous worker lifecycle.

Creates scraper queues via createScraperQueues factory. Defines items queue (bounded mode) with scraperItemJobSchema and images queue with scraperImageJobSchema. Both inherit scraperQueuePolicy for retry, retention, and deduplication settings. Adapter injected via constructor with BullMQ default for production.

createScraperJobContext initializes adapter connection and defines queues. runAutmogProducerJob and runGrimsmoProducerJob enqueue jobs via enqueueScraperJobs utility. Job handlers process bounded queues with concurrency limits. Signal handling for graceful shutdown via abortController.

runAutmogProducer and runGrimsmoProducer fetch source products, normalize payloads, generate stable job IDs, and enqueue to items queue. Grimsmo producer additionally manages sync state mapping and batch reconciliation. Both use enqueueScraperJobs for deduplicated enqueue with replaceCompleted support.

review.overview: PR #403 (feat: stage shared Railway queue, head 143990e) touches three source-grounded layers. First, .railway/railway.ts declares a new sharedQueue variable bound to the same redis variable used by the retained legacyScraperQueue, plus a redisVolume bound to a volume expression, while the scraper service expression keeps its github-sourced and preserve-related bindings. Second, apps/scraper/src/jobs.ts builds job context through createServices, createScraperDb, createRedisConnection, and createScraperQueues, then dispatches per-source producer jobs (runAutmogProducerJob, runGrimsmoProducerJob via isGrimsmoSource) and queue processor jobs. Third, a new packages/queue package (package.json, bullmq.ts, index.ts, contract/test-contract) defines createBullMqQueueAdapter, which opens a Redis connection and defines BullMQ-backed queues; apps/scraper/src/queue/queues.ts calls createBullMqQueueAdapter and defines items/images queues through it. All edges below are parsed source declarations/calls only; none proves deployed runtime infrastructure, storage attachment, or cutover.

review.overview: PR #354 (feat(database): add Pens catalog schema, head 0c3e8fe) adds a normalized Pens domain on top of the existing `product` and `collection_item` tables. The new tables are in `packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts`, with FK-bearing edits in `collection.ts`. Pen, part and refill details use shared-PK subtype tables keyed to `product` (pens.ts:53-55). Pen part subtypes also key to `product_detail_pen_part` (pens.ts:81-83, 89-91, 97-99, 107-109, 122-124). Owned-item pen details do the same against `collection_item` (pens.ts:63-65). A product-configuration model covers slots, choices, rules and requirements (pens.ts:343-515). Refill offerings, compatibility groups and assertions are provenance-backed, with markets and source evidence tables (pens.ts:554-1335). `catalog_terminology_alias` is reshaped to reference a new `catalog_terminology_concept` through a composite concept/namespace FK. The schema barrel, relations map, a Drizzle migration, tests and a catalog service all follow the new shape. Three diagrams are returned. The schema-domain flowchart maps the whole Pens domain, with 32 entities and 54 FKs. ER slice 1 covers the shared-PK pen and refill subtype hierarchies for products and owned items. ER slice 2 covers product configuration, including the exclusive nullable choice carriers, as a separate high-risk domain. Cardinality and PK/FK markers come from the host. They do not include CHECK constraints or the migration's constraint triggers (migration.sql:762-1133).

diagrams.title: ER slice 1: shared-PK Pen, part and refill subtypes for products and owned collection items
ER slice 2: product configuration slots, choices with exclusive nullable carriers, rules, and owned-item selections

changedAreas.summary: `packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts` (+1407 lines) defines the Pens tables. Product detail tables use `productDetailId()`, which is a PK that also references `product.id` (pens.ts:52-55). Clip, tip, top-cap, mechanism and actuator tables additionally reference `product_detail_pen_part.id` on the same PK column (pens.ts:80-126). `product_detail_refill` has two FKs to `product`. One is on `id` alone (pens.ts:52-55). The other is a composite on (`id`, `maker_id`) with name `product_detail_refill_product_maker_fk` (pens.ts:139-143). The composite one references the `product_id_maker_unique` UNIQUE key, not the PK. The relationships catalog lists both (r28, r29). Owned-item pen detail tables use `collectionDetailId()` against `collection_item.id` (pens.ts:62-65, 598-720).

Slots (pens.ts:343) belong to a product and a slot kind (r36, r37). Choices (pens.ts:379-447) have three nullable carrier FKs: `part_product_id` to `product_detail_pen_part` (r38), `product_material_id` to `product_material` (r40) and `finish_option_id` to `finish_option` (r41). The last two are composite FKs that include `product_id` (pens.ts:402-411). A CHECK, `product_configuration_choice_carrier_valid`, uses `num_nonnulls(...) = 1` across the three carriers (pens.ts:434-437). Rules attach to choices (r42, pens.ts:460-467). Requirements link a rule to a required choice (r43, r44, pens.ts:500-515). `collection_item_configuration_selection` has `collection_item_id` (r60), an optional `installed_part_collection_item_id` (r61) and a (`choice_id`, `slot_id`) composite FK to the choice (r62) (pens.ts:722-741).

`refill_offering` references `product_detail_refill` (r45, pens.ts:557-559). Markets are self-related through `catalog_market_containment` (r63, r64, pens.ts:779-784). `catalog_source_evidence` has optional FKs to `catalog_source_listing` and `catalog_market` (r65, r66, pens.ts:831-847). `product_source_listing` joins a product to a listing, with `listing_id` marked unique-inverse (r67, r68, pens.ts:870-875). Offering evidence links offerings to evidence rows (r73, r74, pens.ts:936-941). Group membership joins `refill_compatibility_group` to refills (r77, r78, pens.ts:1121-1126). Compatibility assertions have required `pen_product_id` (r79) and optional tip, group and refill targets (r80-r82, pens.ts:1146-1158). Compatibility evidence has three optional carriers (r83-r85, pens.ts:1241-1251).

`collection.ts` adds `collection_item.serial_number` with a length CHECK (patch lines 13-25). It adds the `product_id_maker_unique` UNIQUE key on `product(id, maker_id)` (collection.ts:368). It adds `product_material_id_product_unique` and `finish_option_id_product_unique`, which the composite choice FKs reference (patch lines 42, 109). `catalog_terminology_alias` loses `canonical_key` and its `product_type.slug` FK. `maker_id` becomes nullable, and `concept_id` is added with a composite FK (`concept_id`, `canonical_namespace`) to `catalog_terminology_concept(id, namespace)` (patch lines 50-81). Alias uniqueness is rewritten with `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` (patch lines 82-84).

The Drizzle migration `20261010021729_pens_catalog_schema/migration.sql` (+1145 lines) holds the DDL, the FK and CHECK statements (for example lines 690-713), and many `CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER` statements (lines 762-1133). The triggers include `validate_pens_product_detail`, `validate_pens_collection_detail` and `validate_product_configuration`. `schema/index.ts` re-exports `pens.js`. `src/index.ts` exports the `PensSchemaRows` and `NewPensSchemaRows` types. `relations.ts` (+587 lines) imports the Pens tables and adds relation entries for them, including a `concept` relation on `catalogTerminologyAlias`. `packages/services/src/db/catalog/index.ts` renames the alias unique-constraint message key to `catalog_terminology_alias_scope_value_unique`. It also resolves a terminology concept before inserting an alias, and joins `catalogTerminologyConcept` when listing aliases.

The changeset marks `@package/database` as minor and `@package/services` as patch. A new `pens-catalog.integration.test.ts` (+371 lines) is added. `fresh-baseline.integration.test.ts`, `material-specifics.integration.test.ts` and the catalog service integration test are edited. `docs/database-schema-diagram.html` gains 1171 lines and is not used as relationship evidence here.

review.overview: PR #354 adds the normalized Pens catalog schema to the pocket-trash database package. New file packages/database/src/schema/pens.ts (review-evidence/6-content.txt) declares product_detail_pen and shared-PK pen part subtypes (clip, tip, top_cap, mechanism, actuator), product_detail_refill, catalog_terminology_concept, product_alias, pen part/nose role assignments, refill compatibility groups and assertions, product configuration slots/choices/rules, refill offerings, collection-detail pen subtypes, collection item configuration selections, and catalog market/source/evidence tables. packages/database/src/schema/collection.ts is reworked: collection_item gains serial_number with a CHECK (collection.ts, 4-patch.txt), product gains the (id, maker_id) composite UNIQUE that refill references, catalog_terminology_alias now references the new concept table via a nullable maker carrier, and product_material/finish_option gain composite UNIQUEs. Drizzle relations (7-content) and the migration (2-content) follow the schema. All relationships below are foreign-key relationships from the frozen visual-relationships-v1 catalogue; cardinalities are host-derived from FK nullability and PK/UNIQUE constraints. Shared-PK subtypes (id FK to parent id) and nullable exclusive carriers (finish_option product_id vs collection_item_id, CHECK-enforced) are preserved as declared.

changedAreas.summary: New Pens catalog schema: product_detail_pen and shared-PK part subtypes product_detail_pen_clip/tip/top_cap/mechanism/actuator all reference product.id and product_detail_pen_part.id (pens.ts 53-124); product_detail_refill references product.id and the (id, maker_id) composite UNIQUE (pens.ts 129-143, anchored by collection.ts 365-366 unique product_id_maker_unique); catalog_terminology_concept, product_alias, pen_part_role_assignment and pen_nose_profile_assignment (pens.ts 161-285, concept referenced by composite concept_id+namespace FKs); refill_compatibility_group (pens.ts 295-315); configuration_slot_kind/product_configuration_slot/choice/choice_rule/choice_requirement (pens.ts 323-515, choices carry nullable part_product_id, product_material and finish_option carriers with junction-mediated composite FKs); refill_tip_style/refill_ink_color/refill_offering (pens.ts 523-567); collection_detail_pen and per-part collection detail subtypes (pens.ts 597-712) plus collection_item_configuration_selection (pens.ts 719-741, two collection_item FKs incl. nullable installed_part carrier); catalog_market containment and catalog source listing/evidence tables with product_source_listing, catalog_source_listing_choice and catalog_source_image (pens.ts 752-909); refill offering evidence/market-status/identifier evidence and compatibility assertion/membership evidence junctions (pens.ts 933-1343).

collection_item gains nullable serial_number with CHECK collection_item_serial_number_valid (4-patch.txt 13-25); product gains unique product_id_maker_unique and index product_maker_id_idx (4-patch.txt 33-34), enabling the composite (id, maker_id) FK target used by product_detail_refill and product_material/finish_option composite UNIQUEs (4-patch.txt 42, 109); catalog_terminology_alias reworked: maker_id becomes nullable, canonical_key/product_type reference removed, concept_id added with composite concept_id+canonical_namespace FK to catalog_terminology_concept (4-patch.txt 53-96) and new scope/preferred uniques.

Drizzle relation definitions added for the pens catalog tables (7-content.txt); schema/index.ts exports ./pens.js (5-content.txt 8); package index re-exports NewPensSchemaRows and PensSchemaRows types (3-content.txt 45, 71).
DDL migration creating the pens catalog tables, composite UNIQUE/FK constraints and CHECK constraints matching pens.ts and the collection.ts constraint additions.

packages/database/test/pens-catalog.integration.test.ts added (371 lines) covering the pens schema; fresh-baseline and material-specifics integration tests updated (8-, 9-content.txt); packages/services/src/db/catalog/index.ts and its integration test updated for pens catalog rows and exact-inclusion relationship handling (11-, 12-content.txt).

review.overview: PR #376 adds material Trends drill-downs across three layers. The database layer gets a new table, public_collection_item_material_trend, and a new boolean on public_trends_generation, has_suppressed_material_values. The services layer gets new trends read and write methods. The web layer gets two server functions, a loader change in the /trends route, and trends page and filter changes. The schema-er diagram shows the four trend entities in packages/database/src/schema/trends.ts. review-relationships.json has no foreign-key relationship records for them, so the diagram has no edges. The FK declarations that exist in source are described in changedAreas with file and line anchors.

diagrams.title: Changed Trends entities (entity nodes only; no FK relationship records in catalog)

changedAreas.summary: New table public_collection_item_material_trend (lines 52-104). Its PK is the single column id (line 55-57). generation_id is NOT NULL with an FK to public_trends_generation.id, ON DELETE CASCADE (lines 58-60). product_type_id (lines 62-65) and material_id (lines 67-70) are nullable FKs to product_type.id and material.id, both ON DELETE RESTRICT. material_specific_id (line 72) is nullable. A composite FK (material_id, material_specific_id) references material_specific(material_id, id), ON DELETE RESTRICT (lines 98-102). A check requires material_id to be non-null whenever material_specific_id is non-null (lines 94-97). A unique index covers generation_id, coalesce(product_type_id,0), coalesce(material_id,0), coalesce(material_specific_id,0) and is_specific_breakdown (lines 83-89). public_trends_generation gains has_suppressed_material_values (lines 39-42). It also has a partial unique index on active where active is true (lines 44-48). public_part_accessory_product_type_trend (lines 107-126) and public_collection_item_product_type_trend (lines 129-150) each declare a composite PK of (generation_id, product_type_id) (lines 120 and 144). Each also declares FKs to public_trends_generation (CASCADE) and product_type (RESTRICT). In the catalog these two tables appear only as context entities.

Creates public_collection_item_material_trend (lines 1-12) and adds has_suppressed_material_values to public_trends_generation (line 14). It creates the scope unique index (line 15). It adds four FK constraints: generation_id to public_trends_generation with CASCADE (line 16), product_type_id to product_types with RESTRICT (line 17), material_id to materials with RESTRICT (line 18), and the composite (material_id, material_specific_id) to material_specific with RESTRICT (line 19). The SQL names the referenced tables product_types, materials and material_specific. The TS schema uses the identifiers productType, material and materialSpecific. snapshot.json was omitted from the evidence as a generated-file pattern.

changedAreas.area: Services layer: packages/services/src/db/trends/index.ts and index exports
changedAreas.summary: The patch adds the PublicMaterialTrend and PublicCollectionMaterialTrends types. It adds getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends, which reads product-type and material data using raw SQL grouping sets. It adds getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends, which selects the active generation from publicTrendsGeneration (patch lines 145-151) and then reads publicCollectionItemMaterialTrend rows by generationId. A tx.insert into publicCollectionItemMaterialTrend appears in the generation-writing code (13-patch lines 328+). packages/services/src/db/index.ts and packages/services/src/index.ts gain 2 lines each. These were not read in detail. An integration test file gains 84 lines.

The /trends route loader adds both calls to its Promise.all, alongside the three existing loaders (8-patch lines 22-41). It passes catalogMaterialTrends and collectionMaterialTrends to TrendsPage. It replaces the onProductTypeChange and selectedProductTypeId props with onSearchChange and search (8-patch lines 60-77).

review.overview: PR #376 adds material Trends drill-downs to the public Trends system. The change introduces a new public_collection_item_material_trend table for privacy-transformed material counts with support for specific-material breakdowns. The public_trends_generation table gains a has_suppressed_material_values column. New service methods support both exact catalog-product material counts and privacy-safe collection-derived material Trends. The schema uses nullable foreign keys for optional product type and material relationships, with composite foreign key constraints for specific-material validation.

Added has_suppressed_material_values column to public_trends_generation (trends.ts:16-104, migration.sql:1-19).

Added getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends and getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends methods. Material Trends support specific-breakdown grouping with item and collector counts rounded to increments of five (packages/services/src/db/trends/index.ts:128-292).

Trends page extended with material drill-down UI. New filter support for productTypeId, materialId, materialSpecificId with isSpecificBreakdown flag (apps/web/src/pages/trends-page.tsx, apps/web/src/lib/catalog-filters.ts).
New endpoints getPublicCollectionMaterialTrends and getPublicCatalogMaterialTrends exposed via catalog-api.ts, delegating to s.db.trends service (apps/web/src/lib/catalog-api.ts:1339-1352).
